why_now: The checklist requires a tolerance declared BEFORE the comparison. A bar chosen after seeing the result is not a gate. Nothing in this repository has yet compared a physical scan against this target's CAD, so this file is written first and is not revised to fit an outcome.

reference.geometry: reconstruction-target-v1-reference.ply, 12000 CAD points with normals and surface_id
reference.scale_adjustment: the scale_x/y/z in prints/physical-print-20260831.json, predeclared for this print before its first scan
not_yet_available: printer, material, nozzle and layer height
reference.consequence: These are ready_for_formal_physical_gate=false in the print record. Results under this file are a DEVELOPMENT metric against CAD-plus-predeclared-shrinkage. They are not a published accuracy claim and must not be quoted as one.

gates.what: Angle between each outer side face (outer_east, outer_west, outer_north, outer_south) and base_top, fitted as planes on the registered scan.
gates.why_this_bar: This is the principal-point test and it needs no calipers and no sphere. A shear x += k*z leaves a plane a plane but rotates its normal: the east/west faces tilt by atan(k) against the top while north/south are untouched. At k=0.3089 - the shear implied if the true cx were the frame centre rather than the factory 42.44 - east-vs-top reads 107.2 rather than 90. A 2-degree bar detects k>=0.035, about a 31-pixel cx error, and is wider than the 1.20-degree loop closure this scan carries.
gates.diagnostic: east/west failing while north/south pass is a shear in x, which is a principal-point or distortion fault, NOT a registration fault.

gates.what: RMS deviation of registered scan points from their own CAD surface, per planar surface_id.
gates.why_this_bar: About 2.3x the 0.65 mm measured per-point noise floor, and above the 1.29 mm that this capture's 1.20-degree held-out loop closure contributes at the target's corner. Tighter would fail on registration error already accounted for; looser would not see an 8%-of-radius shape error.

gates.what: Whether each of the three rails (1.5, 3, 6 mm) and four steps (2, 5, 10, 20 mm) is resolvable in the registered scan.
gates.tolerance: reported, not gated on this pass
gates.why_this_bar: Ungated deliberately. 1.5 mm is 2.3 TSDF voxels and 86% of it is consumed by current loop-closure error, so a fail here would measure known upstream error rather than anything new. It is recorded so the number moves when closure improves.

limitations: Rigid registration to CAD absorbs any global scale error, so nothing here tests the depth scale. The measured -0.49% to -2.26% scale spread is a separate, unclosed question.
A comparison against CAD-plus-predeclared-shrinkage inherits whatever the print actually did. Without repeat caliper readings the ground truth's own uncertainty is unmeasured.
Passing every gate here does not establish dimensional accuracy. It establishes that the scanned shape agrees with the intended shape to the stated bars.
